clue.text: China's Iron Cat could be showing a fault in time

indicators.note: says the letters of the three words could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a Chinese ornamental iron cat is out of place for its supposed period.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's counts here: CHINAS IRON CAT supplies all thirteen letters for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of its proper period, like a wristwatch in a Roman epic, displays a chronological error.

clue.text: Republican misanthrope held by terrorist

indicators.note: one word is gripped inside the other, so the misanthrope sits within the terrorist

parts.note: an anarchist, a bomb-throwing revolutionary of the old cartoon kind
Timon of Athens, Shakespeare's famous hater of mankind

explanation.surface: A republican who hates people is being harboured by a terrorist group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' means the misanthrope sits inside the terrorist's word, not at either end; Timon of Athens is the classic literary hater of mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: A republican opposes rule by a king or queen, which is the stance of an opponent of monarchy.

clue.text: Like group possession

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of 'as good as gold'
a set is a group or collection

explanation.surface: Something is described as like a possession held by a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything valuable that one owns counts on the balance sheet as property.

clue.text: Obstinate nut -and tough

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
strong and tough both mean robust

explanation.surface: A stubborn person is called a tough nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilful person who refuses to be guided is stubborn and self-willed.

clue.text: Cow girl, in awful woe

indicators.note: the girl is placed inside the scrambled letters
an awful version of the word woe is a mangled one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is miserable, perhaps over a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is the verb, to intimidate, not the animal; 'awful' scrambles the woe letters and 'in' puts the girl inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them into submission, much as awe does.

clue.text: Eager to get in time indicator

parts.note: taken as written
in grammar a tense shows when an action happens

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to get inside the timekeeping device.
explanation.definitionFit: An ardent, keenly felt enthusiasm is passionate and fervent.

clue.text: Many in uplifting gear for the moment

indicators.note: the number for many goes inside the other piece
in a down clue lifting up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Plenty of people are wearing elevated clothing for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns KIT into TIK, and C goes in to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech 'just a tick' means just a second, a very short while.

clue.text: Pink, perhaps, in a motor race

parts.note: motor is an old word for a car
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: Something pink appears in a car rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are a group of garden flowers to which this bloom belongs, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Ordinary choice for the outdoor type

explanation.surface: An unremarkable option for someone who loves fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixed phrase means everyday or run-of-the-mill; read literally it offers a choice between two open-air places, a public green or a yard.

clue.text: Will try a catkin!

parts.note: to test is to try out
an ament is a botanical term for a catkin

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to sample a catkin.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will is a legal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: About an old vessel and what it could have held

parts.note: c (circa) is the abbreviation for about, used with dates
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A remark on an ancient ship and what it might have carried.
explanation.definitionFit: The goods a ship carries in its hold are its freight.

clue.text: Lacking lustre and point, son marries

parts.note: mat or matt describes a dull, non-shiny finish
E, east, is a point of the compass
s is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A dull son with no sharpness gets married.
explanation.definitionFit: To mate is to pair up or wed, so the verb fits joining in marriage.

clue.text: The flower of Fred Karno's army

indicators.note: the river is taken out of the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: The best soldier in a famously chaotic army; Fred Karno's army is British slang for a shambolic outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' in crosswords is something that flows, a river; the Arno runs through Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention reads 'flower' as a thing that flows, so a river of Tuscany fits.

clue.text: Soothing influence of the silent castle

indicators.note: being silent means losing what is spoken, so the spoken part is dropped

parts.note: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Scotland

explanation.surface: The calming effect of a quiet castle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment or anything that calms and heals is a soothing remedy.

clue.text: Posed with vase and other things in an orgy

parts.note: sat as in sat for a portrait, posed
an urn is a kind of vase
et alia is Latin for and other things

explanation.surface: Someone posed with a vase and other objects during a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and other things' gives only ALIA, the second half of 'et alia'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman midwinter festival was famed for riotous revelry, so the word now means any wild party.

clue.text: Reason the King of Spain's daughter came to visit me

definitions.text: Reason the King of Spain's daughter came to visit me

parts.words: Reason the King of Spain's daughter came to visit me
parts.note: the nursery rhyme 'I had a little ...' says the princess came all for the sake of the singer's little fruit-bearing plant

explanation.surface: A question about why a Spanish princess paid a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs: 'The King of Spain's daughter came to visit me, and all for the sake of my little' one, which bore a silver nutmeg and a golden pear.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme names this little plant as the whole cause of the royal visit.

clue.text: Siren disturbs MPs' street

indicators.note: to disturb is to throw into disorder, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An enchantress causes uproar on the street where politicians gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren in the figurative sense is a seductive woman who lures men.

clue.text: The first story backs high spirits

indicators.note: backs means the whole sequence is read from the end

parts.note: No. 1, with I for the figure one, is the first
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: The opening story supports a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' reverses NOITALE as a whole, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyful exhilaration is a lifting of the spirits.

clue.text: Imaginative lie — in this kind of language

explanation.surface: A fanciful falsehood, in a particular kind of tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful tale or fabrication; also the family of tongues descended from Latin, such as French or Italian.

clue.text: Frog's in love with delight

parts.note: Frog is slang for French, and en is French for in
amour is French for love

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is in love and thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frog' is old, impolite British slang for French; it governs both pieces, giving 'en amour', in love.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm or captivate someone fills them with fondness and pleasure.

clue.text: Tears back to embrace a French lulu

indicators.note: one piece wraps its arms around the other, so it goes inside
back means this word is read in reverse

parts.note: rents are tears or rips
un is French for a

explanation.surface: Someone tearfully returns to hug a French beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the tears word and 'to embrace' wraps it round the French article; 'lulu' is old slang for a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: A lulu is slang for a remarkable person or thing, here an attractive knockout.

clue.text: Poet, nearly all bones

indicators.note: nearly all of the word is used, one letter being dropped

parts.note: a skeleton is all the bones

explanation.surface: A poet so thin that he is almost all bones.
explanation.walkthrough: John Skelton was a Tudor poet; 'nearly all' drops one E from SKELETON.
explanation.definitionFit: John Skelton was court poet to Henry VIII.

clue.text: This may lead to strikes

indicators.note: the word may lead to another made from its rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A warning that some action could provoke industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: Blows or punches landed are impacts on a target.

clue.text: Direction after wallop is — halt

indicators.note: the direction comes after the wallop in the answer

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or wallop
E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Being hit leaves someone at a standstill.
explanation.definitionFit: Halt in the old sense means limping or crippled, so it means unable to walk properly.

clue.text: Type with a girl

parts.note: a norm is a standard or type

explanation.surface: A kind of man who is with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's name, as in Bellini's opera.

clue.text: Two boys beamed

parts.note: Ray is a boy's name
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A pair of lads smiled broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two boys' gives two names, RAY and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rayed sends out beams, as the sun does.

clue.text: Kid, treated and controlled, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: swayed means influenced or controlled

explanation.surface: A child was dealt with and kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is not a child but kid leather; suede is leather treated to give a napped finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather such as kidskin rubbed to a soft nap becomes this material.

clue.text: KO'd about trifle — overmatched

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second

parts.note: outed in the sense of knocked out
to play with something is to trifle with it

explanation.surface: A boxer flattened while messing about was outclassed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outclassed by a superior opponent is to be beaten by better play.

clue.text: Crocus colour Thoreau's work located in Essex

parts.note: saffron, the orange-yellow from the crocus
Walden is Thoreau's book about life by Walden Pond

explanation.surface: A yellow-orange shade from a book by Thoreau has turned up in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is the place located in Essex, a market town named after its crocus crop.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town in the English county of Essex was named for the crocus grown there for dye.
